muc.title: A biased resume screener
muc.text: A big company once built an AI tool to screen job applications, then had to drop it because it gave lower scores to women's resumes.

muc.title: AI learns from old data
muc.text: That's bias. AI learns from old data, and ten years earlier that company had hired mostly men. AI doesn't mean to be unfair, it just learns the exact slant already in the data.

muc.title: It shows up in many places
muc.text: You'll see bias in many places: ask AI to draw a company director and it often draws a man; ask about your own country's culture and it may answer from a foreign point of view.

muc.title: Be specific to reduce bias
muc.text: To reduce it, say clearly what you want, for example a group of people of different genders, ages and regions. Or ask a follow-up: which side might this answer be leaning toward?

muc.title: Decisions about people
muc.text: For decisions about people, like hiring or lending, let AI suggest, but a real person should review and take responsibility.

muc.title: Try drawing a job
muc.text: Ask AI to draw or describe a doctor and an engineer, see who it assumes by default, then ask for more diversity and compare.
